prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” HVAC company for every situation — the right choice depends on your exact location in the Phoenix metro area, the make/age of your system, whether you need emergency service or a full replacement, and your budget. I can help you pick the best option for your situation. First, some quick paths you can take now, then a checklist and what to ask when you call.

Quick options
- If you want companies that commonly receive strong local reviews in Phoenix (verify current ratings yourself): Goettl Air Conditioning & Plumbing, One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (local franchise), ARS/Rescue Rooter, and Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning. These are large providers that typically offer emergency service, maintenance plans, and warranties — but quality varies by local crew, so verify for your neighborhood.
- If you prefer independent/local techs: search Google/Yelp for “HVAC Phoenix” plus your ZIP, then sort by reviews, recent jobs, and response time.

How to choose — checklist (do these before hiring)
1. License and insurance
   - Ask for their Arizona ROC (Registrar of Contractors) license number and verify it online.
   - Confirm they carry liability insurance and workers’ comp.
2. Certifications and experience
   - NATE certification for technicians is a plus.
   - Experience with your brand/model of AC (e.g., Trane, Carrier, Goodman).
3. Written estimate and scope
   - Get a written estimate with parts, labor, tax, and any extra fees.
   - For replacements, ask for SEER rating and estimated energy savings.
4. Warranties and guarantees
   - Ask about parts and labor warranties and any satisfaction guarantees.
5. References and reviews
   - Look at Google, Yelp, BBB, and local Facebook groups for recent experiences.
6. Emergency service & response time
   - Ask whether they offer 24/7 emergency service and typical arrival window.
7. Pricing & second opinions
   - If a repair is >$500, get a second quote. For full replacements, compare at least 3 written bids.

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed with the Arizona ROC? What’s your license number?
- Are your technicians NATE-certified?
- Do you provide a written estimate? Will you charge a diagnostic/service call fee?
- What’s included in the warranty (parts/labor/how long)?
- How quickly can you come out? Is emergency service available?
- Do you offer maintenance plans and financing if I need a replacement?

What to expect cost-wise (ballpark)
- Service call/diagnostic: $75–$200 (sometimes waived if you proceed with repairs)
- Minor repairs: $150–$600
- Major repairs (compressor, coil): $600–$2,500+
- Full replacement of a central AC: $3,500–$12,000+ depending on size and efficiency

If you want more help
- Tell me your ZIP code, the problem you’re seeing (no cooling, weird noises, frequent cycling, high electric bills), and whether it’s an emergency. I can then suggest a short list of local providers (and a script you can copy/paste to request quotes) or help compare estimates you receive.
